You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# ARC panel marker-count classification

Use when an ARC input has a repeated rectangular grid of panels separated by full-color divider rows/columns, sparse marker cells inside panels, and a smaller output matrix aligned to the panels.

## Procedure
1. Identify full horizontal/vertical divider lines and partition the input into panels, excluding divider cells.
2. For each panel, count cells of the unusual marker color(s), not the separator or base colors.
3. Use all current-instance demo pairs to map each marker count/panel feature to its output value. Verify every output cell; specifically check panels with distinct counts.
4. Apply that mapping to each test panel, with output dimensions equal to the number of panel rows/columns.
5. Validate every output row length and preserve the evidenced fallback value for unobserved counts.

## Solved example and caution
One instance used a 14x7 grid split by divider color 6 into 3x2 panels, each 4x3; the base was 9, marker color 4, and output was 1 exactly for panels with two marker cells, otherwise 9. A distinct demo from the same task used 2x5 panels of size 4x2, base 2, marker 9, with all output values 1; panels contained either one or two markers. The test used divider 3 to form 3x3 panels of size 3x4, base 6, marker 5. Counts were [[2,1,2],[1,2,1],[2,2,2]], and demonstrated count-two => 1, count-one => 6, giving [[1,6,1],[6,1,6],[1,1,1]].

Do not blindly equate same task ID with an identical mapping or layout. Demos may vary colors, panel geometry, and observed marker counts. For the input of 28 separators, it seems like I should have 6 panels, divided into lengths of 4 for the first five and 3 for the last. h=w=28; sep={4,9,14,19,24}; bounds=[(0,4),(5,9),(10,14),(15,19),(20,24),(25,28)]
# Fill straight segments between same-color marker panels, extending endpoints only along the observed aligned pair.
colors={}
def line(color, cells):
 for p in cells:
  colors[p]= color if p not in colors or colors[p]==color else 6
# 3 markers aligned in panel column 2, panel rows 0 and 4
line(3,[(r,2) for r in range(0,5)])
# 2 markers aligned in panel row 1, panel cols 0 and 4
line(2,[(1,c) for c in range(0,5)])
# 2 markers aligned in panel column 0, panel rows 1 and 3
line(2,[(r,0) for r in range(1,4)])
grid=[]
for r in range(h):
 row=[]
 for c in range(w):
  if r in sep or c in sep: v=8
  else:
   ri=next(i for i,(a,b) in enumerate(bounds) if a<=r<b); ci=next(i for i,(a,b) in enumerate(bounds) if a<=c<b)
   v=colors.get((ri,ci),0)
  row.append(v)
 grid.append(row)
import json
print(json.dumps(grid,separators=(',',':')))
print('shape',len(grid),set(map(len,grid)))
